web_evidence.title: East of Eden — Penguin Random House Library Marketing
web_evidence.note: The authorized Chapter 1 excerpt repeatedly uses the narrator's autobiographical I to recall his Salinas Valley childhood.

web_evidence.title: “a great black book”: East of Eden and Gunn’s New Family Physician
web_evidence.note: Robert DeMott's scholarly article explicitly describes Steinbeck's modulation of first- and third-person points of view and his entry into his ancestral story.

web_evidence.title: The Reader’s Story: The Original East of Eden as a Postmodern “Fictory”
web_evidence.note: Steven Mulder's Ohio University MA thesis analyzes third-person narration repeatedly disrupted by a participating first-person I and documents the narrator appearing both as I and externally as John.

web_evidence.title: East of Eden Summary and Study Guide
web_evidence.note: The structural overview states that most of the novel is third-person while the narrator has separate first-person philosophical and historical sections.

web_evidence.title: East of Eden: Key Facts
web_evidence.note: The point-of-view description identifies third-person storytelling across multiple characters together with frequent first-person authorial intrusions.

person_note: The novel combines sustained third-person family-saga narration with recurring first-person autobiographical and authorial sections spoken by a narrator who belongs to the Hamilton family history. The authorized opening verifies the memoir-like I, while quote passages about Cathy, Tom, Charles, and other characters expose substantial third-person narration; scholarly whole-book analysis explicitly describes these modulations. Apparent contrary first-person quotes such as q00803 are character speech, while q00795, q00797, q00822, q00847, q00861, q00863, and q00865 belong to the narrator despite several upstream dialogue or gnomic buckets. The only conceptual uncertainty is whether this is described as one hybrid narrator or two grammatical modes; under the project rule that sustained base sections in different persons are ALTERNATING, the structure resolves to ALTERNATING.
